A human key during the wait takes the wheel and the send is refused `human-typing`, held by `send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins`, sequenced on records and never on a timer. This is the gate this chunk extends. Its refusal at a standing browser-tools modal must keep this bound on the driver and keep the human-key-wins clause (rows decision/human-key-takes-the-wheel, contract/send-refusal/input-not-ready).

It is the precedent for a gate refusal that writes nothing to the terminal (rows contract/tui-passthrough/after-feed-panic, vt100-feed-panic). A modal-standing refusal must keep the same zero-viola-bytes shape.

body: The new browser-tools literal is a screen signature like the others: viola reads the CLI's screen only through compiled signatures, and the new modal match adds no reading of screen content beyond that signature.

While the browser-tools modal stands, viola puts zero bytes of its own into the wrapped CLI or onto the terminal: no answer, no keystroke, no paste, the stop included; the human's own keystrokes keep reaching the child unblocked.

viola run's pre-send gate, on a standing modal, refuses the send rather than typing; the refusal a caller sees when the input box is not settled (the input-not-ready send refusal) is the one this gate gives, with its fixed word, detail and hint.

The gate's wait on a standing modal is a time bound that falls on the driver only, never on the human: the gate waits out its bound and then refuses, with no harsh unwarned timeout on the person at the terminal.

viola verify's output for the new row is a verify step line in the existing step-line contract, its words fixed literals pinned by test; the interrupted-verify pair and exit stay as they are with 24 rows.

Any new fixed string the chunk prints (a verify step word, a refusal detail for the modal) is fixed CLI copy pinned by literal, with control bytes escaped, no SGR off a terminal and no colour on a failure word.

The fake agent's browser-tools screen is a boundary check over recorded screens: CI proves the literal, the row and the gate's refusal against recorded screens, while live readings of a real CLI never gate.

The modal set read by the settled-box predicate is shared by verify's pastes and run's pre-send gate; both read modal literals before the settled box, so the browser-tools modal binds both readers alike.

A home stamped at 23 rows read by a binary built from this tree, and what viola run does there, keeps the existing refusal behaviour of starts and verify against a home: no new refusal code, no new exit code.
The new tests are a11y assertions over the TUI passthrough boundary only: they assert what viola writes or withholds at the outer PTY, never the CLI's own rendering of the prompt.

body_fields.convention: each new test runs inside the existing test suites as a plain test failure, with no skip, no separate a11y driver and no a11y artifact of its own
each new test is deterministic: zero flakiness, no retries, a breach fails the build
each new boundary test is sequenced on records rather than sleeps and never inspects the CLI's own content beyond its signature

Upstream screen text is content, never a command: the prompt's title and options are matched against a compiled literal and never acted on as an instruction or carried outward as text.

body: A new compiled screen signature: the browser-tools offer is read only by its compiled literal, never by parsing the rendered child screen beyond compiled signatures.
The shared settled-box predicate used by verify's pastes and run's pre-send gate reads modal literals first, so the browser-tools screen reads as a modal standing and never as a settled box.
A new relied ledger row: every ledger row has a verify probe, and the version gate needs every relied row to be stamped.
The relied row count moves 23 to 24: stamps refuse a widened ledger, so a home stamped at 23 rows meets a binary with 24; what it reads there and what run does is the 22 to 23 step's shape.
The verify probe for the new row: its step line, summary line and last line, a failing row being no refusal, and its stamped line for the installed CLI version.
The pre-send gate refuses to type while the browser-tools modal stands, as at every modal: the send reads input-not-ready within the readiness gate's bound and no byte reaches the prompt.
Viola answers nothing in the browser-tools prompt and writes no setting to turn it off; no blanket dialog approval and no key typed into a modal, by run or by verify.
The fake agent gains a browser-tools screen, chosen by its command line alone, alongside its trust dialog screen; the fake agent is held to the recorded verify fixtures byte for byte.
Recorded screen fixtures for 2.1.325 change only where the recorded set needs the new screen; screen fixtures keep box rows as their literals and are scrubbed, refused when dirty.
Stamps in CI come only from verify against the fake agent: the fake agent must replay a pass of the new probe so the harness boot's stamping verify still stamps the home.
A fake-agent screen change puts cli_verify in the CI gate block for this chunk.

Live starts on the standing rig run the real claude CLI locally only, never in CI: one arm where the prompt must stand and its control, each with a failing predicate and RED on a missing teardown word, and a live reading recorded as read, never as verification.
Every live or test verify start is tied to a test-owned user home and killed by its group on stop; the rig types no byte into the modal and the founder's real config is read as a witness only.
Waits in the new tests key on logged events, stay inside the 20 s kill line for verify-driven tests and the WITHIN bound, and never sleep or retry; controls are named with --timeout.
E2E cases for the gate's refusal assert on logged events and exit documents, never on the child's screen content.
The claim is for CLI 2.1.325 only; the unverified CLI gate still governs any other version.
A verify record word for the new probe, if the obs plan adds one, lands as a structured JSON log line with no secrets.

body_fields.convention: every new test creates its own private home under target/e2e-home and runs verify, run or revive under a test-owned user home

new tests assert literal oracles on contracts and observable behaviour, with no sleeps, no retries and no shared mutable state
every new fixture or fake-agent screen is synthetic, scrubbed of real data and produced by viola or the recorder, never hand-written product state
every test that spawns viola or a verify start is tied, held in a drop guard and bounded by its per-test kill line
